transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan R. (Redwood AE), Samir P. (Redwood SE), Nina A. (Redwood PM), Lydia C., Marcus V., Tobias G., Priya K.

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood ran through the Optimize console with a focus on prefetch / KV prefix caching recommendations for Mesa Retail's personalized product recommendations use case. Discussed batching, concurrency, session affinity, and cost model tradeoffs. Customer is interested in a short pilot to validate latency and tokens-per-recommendation savings. Security questions surfaced about KMS and data residency.

----- Transcript -----
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Samir, our SE, and Nina who owns Optimize. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Lydia: Good, thanks. We, uh, appreciate the walkthrough. We've been digging into the latency numbers you published and we want to understand real savings when we apply prefix/KV caching to our recommendation flows.
[00:22] Samir: Great — stoked to show you. Quick agenda: 1) short demo of the Console Optimize tab, 2) look at batching and prefetch configs, 3) run through cost model scenarios with your workload assumptions, and 4) next steps for a pilot. Does that sound right?
[00:35] Tobias: Yes, that works. I just want to make sure we cover any dedicated vs hosted constraints — data residency and KMS primarily.
[00:42] Jordan: We'll cover that in the security Q&A near the end. If it's okay, Samir will drive the demo.
[00:48] Samir: Cool. I'm sharing my screen — tell me if you can't see the console.
[01:05] Samir: OK, Console > Optimize. This page surfaces our recommendations produced from runtime traces: suggested batch sizes, prefix cache TTLs, and KV prefetch heuristics. For Mesa's case we loaded the sample trace you provided last week, so these numbers are pre-populated.
[01:25] Marcus: Small note — the trace was anonymized, some tokens got stripped, hope that's fine.
[01:30] Samir: Totally fine, we only need the shape of requests and the sequence lengths. So first thing: recommended batch size is 8 for your 32-token average completions under our hosted models. That reduces per-token amortized overhead while keeping 95th percentile latency under your 150ms SLO in the simulated run.
[01:50] Lydia: Wait, batch size 8 — what's the real impact on latency p95? Our p50 is already ~60ms.
[01:58] Samir: Good question. In our sim: baseline (no batching) p95 was 210ms. With batch=8 continuous batching, p95 dropped to 170ms, but with prefix cache on hot keys the p95 drops to 120ms. So there's a sweet spot: batching helps throughput/cost but can add tail latency if caches miss.
[02:22] Tobias: Are these numbers on hosted or a dedicated instance? We need to compare apples to apples.
[02:28] Samir: These sims ran on Redwood hosted instances with the model variant that matches your quality constraints — the console marks it as rdx-large-v1 in the trace (sometimes transcribed as redx, sorry if that sounds off). On Dedicated, with reserved capacity, the batch behavior changes slightly because of predictable concurrency; p95 is usually ~10–20% lower in stable dedicated pools.
[02:49] Priya: How does session affinity play into this? Our product recommender tends to re-query in a user session and we want cache hits for user histories.
[02:58] Samir: Sessionization is crucial. For Mesa, we recommended a session-affinity TTL of 30 minutes for the KV prefix cache. That increases hit rates for returning users and reduces tokens-per-recommendation by ~35% in the sim. The tradeoff is cache memory and potential staleness; we discussed TTL tuning in the Optimize UI.
[03:20] Jordan: A few of you asked about tokens-per-recommendation — Samir, can you flip to the cost-simulation tab?
[03:28] Samir: Sure. Here: cost model inputs. We modeled three scenarios: baseline (no cache), partial-prefetch (prefetch 20% of the top prefixes), and aggressive-prefetch (prefetch 60% of prefixes + longer TTL). For Mesa's traffic pattern, partial-prefetch gives ~25% token cost reduction and aggressive up to ~47% but with increased KV storage and higher prefetch lookup counts.
[03:55] Lydia: Those storage costs — do they show up prominently? We need TCO not just token savings.
[04:02] Samir: Yup, the workbook includes an amortized storage + prefetch API call line item. For your traffic, prefetch calls add about 0.8% to API call volume in the aggressive case but storage increases are small relative to token savings. We'll share the sheet so you can change pricing assumptions (e.g., if you use a different cloud KMS or have a different token price).
[04:22] Marcus: Does prefetch happen synchronously in the request path or is it async? I worry about added latency.
[04:28] Samir: Prefetch is async when safe — console suggests an LRU prefetcher that warms the KV cache ahead of requests. For misses on cold keys, you pay the lookup cost in-path. That's why we recommended a hybrid: prefetched hot prefixes + fallbacks to model variants (smaller quantized variant) to preserve latency SLOs.
[04:49] Tobias: Smaller model fallback — is that automatic? I remember you mentioned model routing before.
[04:54] Samir: Yes, routing policies can be set: route by latency, cost, or region. You can configure automatic fallback to a quantized variant (e.g., rdx-small-q4) if latency exceeds thresholds. Console shows simulated output quality impact as well.
[05:10] Lydia: The simulation quality numbers — how accurate are they? We can't degrade recommendations too much.
[05:16] Nina: We run A/B evals tied to your prompt sets. In the Optimize tab you can provide a testset of prompt/completion pairs and we compute delta BLEU / heuristic similarity. It's not perfect, but it flags big regressions. For Mesa we had less than 1% delta in top-k overlap when moving to the quantized fallback in the sim.
[05:37] Jordan: Quick pause — Marcus, Priya, any infra constraints on your side around outbound prefetch calls or KMS?
[05:45] Marcus: We prefer VPC endpoints and KMS keys managed in our account. Also need audit logs for all prefetch and cache-ejection events for compliance.
[05:55] Jordan: That aligns with Redwood Private — we can run the control plane in your VPC and integrate your KMS; audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We'll drop the architecture note in the follow-up.
[06:04] Priya: How about encryption in transit between the KV store and the model runtime?
[06:09] Samir: TLS by default. For on-prem deployments we support mTLS and HSM-backed keys for extra assurance.
[06:16] Lydia: Back to the cost model: are token prices customizable? Our procurement uses negotiated token rates with another vendor and we need side-by-side.
[06:24] Samir: Yes, you can input your negotiated rates into the workbook. The console uses our public pricing by default but we always export a CSV so you can plug in your numbers.
[06:33] Tobias: If we want to pilot, what's the minimal scope? We don't want to do a big lift.
[06:40] Samir: Minimal pilot: 1) provide 24–72h traffic sample + SLOs, 2) Redwood loads traces and proposes prefetch TTLs and batch configs, 3) we run a shadow pilot behind your routing for 1–2 weeks with metrics collection, and 4) we review cost/latency/quality and agree go/no-go. We can run this on hosted or Dedicated depending on your compliance needs.
[07:05] Lydia: For the shadow pilot, do we need to proxy traffic or can we replicate?
[07:10] Samir: Either. We commonly do a replicate mode where we mirror requests to Redwood for simulation plus a small percentage routed live for end-to-end latency. That keeps production risk low.
[07:21] Jordan: I'm going to show one more Optimize feature — the heatmap of prefix hit rates.
[07:27] Samir: Heatmap shows hot prefixes by frequency and average response size; here you can click a prefix and see per-minute hit rate and suggested prefetch window. For Mesa the top 150 prefixes cover ~62% of traffic — that's where prefetch gives biggest ROI.
[07:50] Lydia: 62% coverage on 150 prefixes — that's pretty compact. What's the memory footprint for that?
[07:56] Samir: In the sim it's about 12GB of KV storage (including overhead). We show a breakdown: keys, avg value size, TTL churn.
[08:04] Marcus: Is eviction LRU or LFU? We need predictable behavior for hot user sessions.
[08:09] Samir: Eviction policy is configurable; we recommend LRU for sessionized workloads but LFU is available for heavily skewed long-tail prefixes. You can also pin a small set of critical prefixes.
[08:21] Tobias: Can we set hard cost limits that throttle prefetch behavior?
[08:25] Samir: Yes, Optimize supports guardrails. You can set max prefetch calls per minute and a budget cap; the prefetcher will back off once thresholds are hit. Those rules are in the console under "Prefetch policy".
[08:36] Lydia: A practical question: we use a mix of catalog-based and behavior-based prefixes. How do we avoid stale recommendations after catalog updates?
[08:45] Nina: We surface a freshness metric and recommend shorter TTLs for catalog-driven prefixes plus an explicit invalidation hook you can call from your pipeline after a catalog update. That's one of the few times you'd do an explicit invalidation rather than relying on TTL.
[08:59] Marcus: Let's talk about measurement — which metrics should we watch during the pilot?
[09:04] Samir: Key metrics: cache hit rate by prefix cohort, tokens-per-recommendation, end-to-end p50/p95 latency, model quality (A/B top-k overlap), prefetch API volume, and KV storage. Console will stream these and you can hook them to your metrics backend.
[09:20] Lydia: Anything else we should be wary of?
[09:24] Samir: Watch for oscillation — aggressive prefetch + small TTLs can cause churn if traffic patterns change quickly. We recommend a conservative warm-up: start with partial-prefetch (hot prefixes only) and monitor hit rates before widening.
[09:36] Tobias: Ok — procurement will ask for SOC2, SSO, and audit logs. Are those in the standard package?
[09:42] Jordan: Yes, Redwood's hosted product is SOC2 Type II; we support SAML SSO and SSO provisioning, RBAC, and audit logs. For Private we sign an enterprise contract with additional controls. I'll attach the security pack.
[09:53] Priya: Are we able to route a subset of traffic to Dedicated GPUs for the pilot to test carriage?
[09:59] Samir: Absolutely — we can do hybrid routing. Route X% to Dedicated, rest to hosted, and console will aggregate the metrics.
[10:07] Lydia: You mentioned fallback to quantized models earlier — will that need retraining or is it purely runtime switch?
[10:13] Samir: Purely runtime switch between model variants. No retrain required; just the quantized weights produce slightly different outputs which we validate in the A/B eval.
[10:23] Jordan: Quick check — any regulatory or data residency questions not yet covered?
[10:28] Tobias: We operate in EU and US; customer data must stay in-region. We also need to know how long request logs are retained.
[10:35] Samir: Console shows retention controls; you can set request log retention per-project. For Private deployments you can keep logs in your VPC. Will include retention options in the follow-up.
[10:45] Lydia: Let's talk budget: if we run a 2-week pilot and then scale, what's a rough monthly delta in cost?
[10:52] Samir: Depends on how aggressive you get with prefetch. Our sim shows partial-prefetch reduces monthly token bill by ~20% but adds a small storage + prefetch call cost. Net delta often favors prefetch; we'll put numbers in the workbook for your traffic shape.
[11:06] Jordan: OK, time for a short live scenario — Samir, can you toggle the prefetch slider to show simulated cost impact in real time?
[11:12] Samir: Live now... moving from 20% to 60% hot-prefix prefetch... you can see the estimated token savings curve and the prefetch call increase. There's also a projected p95 impact line; here, at 60% it's still within your 150ms SLO in the hosted sim.
[11:32] Marcus: Nice. That helps. A small nit: can the console export the simulation as JSON for our internal finance tool?
[11:38] Nina: Yes — export CSV and JSON are both available. We'll include the export in the follow-up.
[11:44] Lydia: Two more quick questions: 1) support SLAs during pilot? 2) who owns the instrumentation?
[11:50] Jordan: For pilots we provide dedicated SE hours and a 4-hour response for production incidents during the pilot window. Instrumentation is collaborative — Redwood provides SDKs and tracing hooks, but your platform team will wire metrics to your backend.
[12:02] Priya: That seems reasonable.
[12:06] Samir: Also, one thing I wanted to flag: if you have cold-start heavy traffic segments (e.g., new user cohort), we recommend blending lookahead caching where we prefetch prefix candidates based on a small ML model rather than pure frequency. It mitigates cold-start misses.
[12:22] Lydia: Interesting — can that be part of the pilot?
[12:25] Samir: Yes, as an add-on experiment. We'll scope it after the initial 2-week run.
[12:30] Tobias: Anything on compliance about prefetch storing PII? We need to ensure keys/values don't contain raw PII.
[12:36] Samir: We recommend hashing or tokenizing PII before storage. Console also supports a redaction hook. We'll note it in the security attachment.
[12:44] Jordan: We're around the 40-minute mark — let's do a brief recap and agreed next steps.
[12:50] Jordan: Recap: 1) Console's Optimize gives batch + prefetch recommendations tuned to your traces; 2) partial-prefetch looks like the low-risk first step saving ~20–30% tokens; 3) session affinity + 30min TTL recommended; 4) pilot scope: 1–2 week shadow run with replicated traffic; 5) security & VPC/KMS options available.
[13:15] Lydia: Sounds good. Please include the detailed cost workbook and the recording.
[13:18] Jordan: Action items — Jordan to send workbook + recording, Samir to draft pilot config, Lydia to share traffic sample and SLOs.
[13:28] Tobias: We'll also want the SOC2 and data retention docs.
[13:31] Jordan: Noted. We'll attach them.
[13:35] Priya: One last question — who is the single point of contact on Redwood for the pilot?
[13:40] Jordan: Me — Jordan Reyes. Samir will be the technical lead.
[13:44] Marcus: Great.
[13:46] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by Tuesday with the workbook.
[13:50] Lydia: Thanks, bye.
[13:52] Tobias: Bye.

----- End transcript -----

Post-call notes (handwritten by AE):
- Customer is motivated by cost savings but very sensitive to quality drift; must keep >95% top-k similarity.
- Prefer VPC/KMS integration; audit logs required.
- Pilot likely to be 2 weeks shadow + small live %; aim to finalize scope by next Tue.

References mentioned in call:
